title: Devil Is in the Edges: Learning Semantic Boundaries From Noisy Annotations (STEAL)
mechanism: A thinning loss forces a single response peak along the edge normal, and active alignment moves noisy 1-2 px edge labels toward the true boundary by level-set evolution during training.
adaptation: Treat crack as an edge class. Every N steps, snap each crack label polyline to the ridge of the current crack logit within +/-2 px, keeping the source's width convention, and add the normal-direction NMS loss on the crack channel only. The released code is old inference code (PyTorch 0.4), so we would reimplement it.
min_experiment: Arm: PF + periodic label snapping + NMS loss, 5 seeds. Baseline: PF, 5 seeds. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, crack pixel precision. Kill if crack IoU falls more than 0.012 below baseline, or if relF1@2 shows no detectable difference.
evidence: R (abstract): edge datasets carry label noise that pushes detectors toward thick predictions; STEAL improves on a CASENet backbone and can refine coarse labels. Its edges are 1-2 px wide, the closest structural analogue to our crack labels.
prior_overlap: Partial. Offset-tolerant CE (n.d.) took a per-pixel min over shifts. STEAL instead re-aligns labels persistently to the image or model ridge and adds a thinning loss, which was not tested. Soft clDice and Skeleton Recall are different mechanisms.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply the normal-NMS loss to crack only, normal from the orientation target; replace level sets with a +-2 px 1D search along the normal for the best-scoring label position.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF + normal-NMS loss + 1D alignment vs PF; metric relF1@2, width ratio, strict IoU; kill if relF1@2 +<0.01 or width ratio <0.8.

alt_notes.adaptation: Take the normal direction from the orientation of the label skeleton and apply the NMS loss to crack logits. Replace the level set with a simple snake: every k steps, move each crack label curve to the model's ridge within 2 px. This is the canonical align-while-training baseline.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + NMS loss + periodic label alignment, 5 seeds. Baseline: house at 100% labels. Metrics: crack IoU, relF1@2, component recall. Kill if all are n.d.

alt_notes.adaptation: Normals from label skeleton orientation; NMS loss on crack logits; every k steps move each crack label curve to the model ridge within 2 px using a simple snake instead of the level set.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + NMS loss + periodic label alignment, 5 seeds; baseline house. Metrics crack IoU, relF1@2. Kill if both n.d. About 12 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Apply the NMS loss across the crack normal (orientation from label polyline) so the model gives one peak per crack; replace level sets with a 1D search of +-2 px along the normal for the best-scoring label position.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm = PF + normal-NMS loss + 1D alignment on crack; baseline = PF; 5 seeds + CV; metrics relF1@2, crack IoU, predicted width. Kill if relF1@2 gain < 0.01 and IoU drops.

alt_notes.adaptation: Every 2k steps move each crack label pixel to the argmax of p(crack) within 2 px along the local normal, preserving connectivity, and keep the updated label. SEAL bipartite matching (ECCV 2018) is a simpler implementation.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + active alignment on crack labels. Baseline: house. Metric: relF1@2 primary, strict IoU secondary. Kill if relF1@2 gain < +0.01 or strict IoU drop > 0.02. About 6 GPU-h.

alt_notes.adaptation: Model-in-the-loop snapping: every 2k steps move each crack polyline along its normal within 2 px to the argmax of p(crack) blended with ridge strength, re-dilate to source width. Compare with fixed filter snapping.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Only if the ridge-snap arm passes. Arm: model-in-the-loop snap; baseline: ridge-snap arm. Kill if n.d. vs ridge-snap.

alt_notes.adaptation: Use the normal-direction max-response loss as an auxiliary crack loss: along each label skeleton normal (5 px profile) the predicted crack probability should peak once. Skip level-set alignment (covered by the snake arm).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house + normal-max auxiliary loss on crack, 5 seeds. Baseline: house. Metric: clean-49 crack IoU and pixel precision. Kill: crack IoU under +0.012 with no precision gain.

alt_notes.adaptation: Align jittered 1-2 px crack labels toward the dark ridge during training (half of label points are > 1 px off the ridge), keep each source's width; NMS loss to control predicted width. Test labels stay jittered, so judge on relF1@2 and width, not only strict IoU.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: house training with label alignment step every k iterations. Baseline: house. Metrics: crack relF1@2, crack IoU, predicted width per source on 5-fold CV. Kill: relF1@2 < +0.005 and IoU drop > 0.01.
